text: Outer / inner colours; LCA; contraction with DSU.

In a general graph (一般图 , not bipartite) augmenting paths still decide maximum matching (Berge), but searching for them breaks on odd cycles: the alternating search can reach a vertex by paths of both parities. Edmonds' blossom algorithm (带花树) contracts such an odd cycle (a "blossom") into one vertex, keeps searching, and expands it when an augmenting path is found. O(n³) (P6113).

BFS from a free vertex, colouring vertices "outer" and "inner" alternately. An edge between two outer vertices closes a blossom: find their LCA in the search forest, and merge the cycle into one base vertex with DSU; inner vertices of the blossom become outer and join the queue. Reaching a free vertex from an outer one = augment along the stored pairs.

The lca walk must jump by pre[match[x]] (two steps of the alternating path) and compare bases; forgetting find() there produces wrong blossoms that only show up on graphs with nested odd cycles.
Bipartite graphs never need any of this: use Hungarian or flow (拓展篇第1章).
Random skew-symmetric matrix; rank = 2 × matching.

Tutte matrix (Tutte 矩阵): for an undirected graph build an n × n matrix with A[u][v] = xuv and A[v][u] = −xuv for every edge, 0 elsewhere. Tutte's theorem: its rank is twice the maximum matching size (as a matrix of symbols). Fill the symbols with random numbers modulo a large prime and the rank is correct with high probability (Schwartz–Zippel).

This gives the matching size with one Gaussian elimination, O(n³), and about 30 lines, much shorter than blossom. Finding the matching itself is possible with more linear algebra but blossom (above) is the usual tool for that.

Key points to memorise
1. Berge: matching is maximum ⇔ no augmenting path.
2. Odd cycles break bipartite search: contract them (blossoms).
3. BFS: outer / inner colours; outer–outer edge ⇒ blossom at their LCA.
4. Reaching a free vertex ⇒ flip the path; O(n³).
5. Tutte matrix: random x_uv, −x_uv; rank / 2 = max matching (w.h.p.).
